newsitem.title: CANADA: Sask Wheat Pool loses cattle court case.
newsitem.headline: Sask Wheat Pool loses cattle court case.

text.p: A Manitoba rancher has defeated Canada's largest grain handler in a court battle over their corporate names, both parties said on Friday.
"It amounts to a David and Goliath scenario. I registered the name first and there's been some confusion with respect to the name," Steinbach-area rancher Brent Futz told Reuters.
Futz operates a 160 cow/calf operation in southeast Manitoba and incorporated his Heartland Cattle Company in March 1994.
Saskatchewan Wheat Pool registered its Heartland Livestock Services in October 1996 in Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta.

"It would be quite easy for members of the farming community to believe that the companies were either related and/or the same company," Manitoba Court of Queen's Bench Justice Daniel Kennedy wrote in his May 30 judgement.
SWP and Heartland Livestock Services officials declined to say whether they would appeal the decision or change the firm's name in Manitoba.
SWP's lawyer was not available for comment.
